_note: How a services firm commercialises a Lyzr product. The second half of discovery: the capability path asks what work a partner could sell next, this one asks which Lyzr product their existing business is already shaped to resell, deploy or run. Every `capabilities` line is read off the product's own page; nothing here is written from memory. `requires` is the gate: a play may only be proposed when the partner's capability map actually shows that signal, because an industry match is not a reason to recommend a product. Each offering also carries the customer problems it addresses, two or three services a partner could charge for, and the commercial or technical restrictions on it. Restrictions are the line between what the product can technically do and what we are entitled to promise: unpublished licensing terms and ship dates belong there, not in a card.

offerings.name: OpenController
offerings.one_line: The control plane over every agent a client is already running, wherever it runs.
capabilities: Discovers agents across clouds, clusters and on-premises, including ones nobody registered
Issues workload identity to every agent through the client's existing identity provider
Enforces policy in the request path: access control, rate limits, model routing and guardrails
Gates releases on multi-turn, red-team and regression evals with evidence per version
Traces every action with cost, quality and ownership, exported to their observability tools
complements: Agent or GenAI delivery work already in production at clients
Cloud platform engineering and landing zone work
Security, identity or compliance practices

requires.why: A control plane is only sellable to a firm whose clients already have agents running, or who runs the platform those agents would run on.

implementation.offer: Find every agent the client is running, put identity and policy on each one, and hand back an inventory with an audit trail

managed.offer: Run the control plane for them: policy changes, release gating and the evidence pack their risk function asks for

offerings.buyer: CISO, Head of Platform Engineering or Chief Risk Officer
offerings.trigger: Agents are in production that nobody has inventoried, or an audit date is on the calendar
prerequisites: The client has agents running somewhere, built on anything
An existing identity provider to authenticate against
Someone accountable for AI risk
do_not_recommend_when: The partner has never delivered anything into production for a client
Their clients have no agents and no plan for any, so there is nothing to govern
The partner only advises and does not operate anything
customer_problems: Agents are running in production that nobody has inventoried or made anyone accountable for
An audit asks who approved a model change and there is no record of it
Each team governs its own agents differently, so policy means something different in each one

sellable_services.name: Agent estate discovery
sellable_services.client_gets: A list of every agent running, with an owner against each one

sellable_services.name: Policy and identity rollout
sellable_services.client_gets: Every agent call authenticated and checked against policy before it reaches a system

sellable_services.name: Managed agent operations
sellable_services.client_gets: Release gating, incident triage and an evidence pack their risk function accepts

restrictions: Needs an identity provider to authenticate against
Governs agents wherever they run; it does not build them

revenue.implementation: Find every agent the client is running, put identity and policy on each one, and hand back an inventory with an audit trail
revenue.recurring: Run the control plane for them: policy changes, release gating and the evidence pack their risk function asks for

offerings.name: SuperFlow

Workflow and BPM work
Existing RPA or iPaaS estates

managed.offer: Own the orchestration layer and the runbook, billed per workflow per month

offerings.trigger: A workflow that works in testing keeps failing in production, or approvals are being handled over email beside the system

Access to the systems each step has to call

The partner has no integration or process practice to attach it to
customer_problems: A workflow that passes testing keeps failing somewhere in production
Approvals happen over email beside the system, so nobody can reconstruct a decision
A crash mid-run means the whole process is restarted by hand
